root_idea.summary: The best-supported semantic orientation is freshness, newness, moisture, and renewed vitality.
root_idea.development: The freshness/newness branch extends to making things fresh or fragrant, while the lexicon also records separate movement, praise, bodily, material, and culinary branches.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested adjective with the normalized classical citation form طَرِيّ.

senses.definition: Fresh, newly fresh, juicy, or moist.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic usage, it qualifies flesh or meat, including fish, emphasizing freshness and juiciness or moisture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become fresh, juicy, or moist; to become new or renewed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The new-or-renewed use is specifically reported for the variant طَرِىَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come from a distant place, or to come upon people unexpectedly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may describe coming forth upon people without their knowledge; it is reported as a dialectal variant of طَرَأَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To advance or come forward; also to pass by, go, or go away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The movement and departure uses are reported for the forms طَرَا and طَرِىَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make something fresh, juicy, or moist.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The use includes refreshing or moistening a garment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make perfume, aloes-wood, or food fragrant by mixing in aromatics.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction describes scenting or enhancing the item through admixture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To plaster or coat a building with clay or mud.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is reported as a dialectal use of the Form II verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To praise, commend, or eulogize someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported nuances include praise that renews the person's mention; some authorities extend the term to excessive, unfounded, or falsely exaggerated praise.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make honey thicken or coagulate.
To suffer indigestion or heaviness of the stomach after eating much, becoming distended in the belly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related form اِظْرَوْرَى is also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Surface material unlike the substance of the earth, such as pebbles, small stones, and dust; in a reported broader use, created things beyond reckoning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term occurs in a comparison pairing such surface material with moist earth.
This is a reported and textually uncertain use; the lexical note suggests that the transmitted form may reflect طَارِئٌ instead.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A table used for eating, or a dish or plate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The transmitted pronunciation varies, and another form with a doubled ر is reported as a dialectal pronunciation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A food made from softened starch or flour, formed like threads.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The item is identified with regional preparations such as a threadlike starch food.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The first stage and quickness of youth; a state of youthfulness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It can describe the youthful state or early phase of anything.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Aloes-wood or another aromatic preparation rendered fragrant by added perfume, ambergris, or similar substance; also a scented washing preparation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is used for aromatic material and preparations compounded with fragrances.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Restored to a good condition of body or property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is reported as a figurative or tropical expression.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pointer-only cross-reference to the preceding entry.

cautions: The reported stranger sense under طَرِيّ is textually uncertain and may reflect طَارِئٌ; it is retained as a cautiously reported Classical use.
Lane's references to the Quranic freshness sense use historical citation notation; the modern examples here rely only on the independently supplied QAC locations 16:14 and 35:12.
